# Jocelyn Benson Watchdog File

**Subject:** Jocelyn Benson, Democratic nominee for Governor of Michigan, 2026. Sitting Michigan Secretary of State since January 1, 2019. Running mate Winnie Brinks. Opponent John James, MI-john-james.
**Compiled:** October 23, 2026 for the On Point Politics watchdog database, onpointpolitics.us. Research tier: Tier 2 compact.
**Data cutoff:** October 23, 2026. Latest filing reviewed covers July 20 to August 24, 2026.
**Next scheduled data drop:** Michigan pre-general campaign statements, which Bridge Michigan said were due at the end of the week of October 19, 2026. They were not reviewed for this file.

## Bottom line up front

Benson is the fundraising leader in an open seat race, with about $5.9 million cash on hand on August 24, 2026 against $1.5 million for James, and Benson and allied groups were booked to outspend James on television by roughly $23 million to $1 million heading into October, per AdImpact data reported by Bridge Michigan. Her money is broad and capped: Michigan limits gifts to $8,325 from individuals and $83,250 from PACs, so no single donor dominates her committee the way the DeVos family dominates the pro James super PAC. Four interests combine real money with a live decision on her desk.

1. **Data centers and the Saline Township project.** Her husband, Ryan Friedrichs, is a vice president of development at Related Companies, whose Related Digital is developing the $7 billion, 1.4 gigawatt OpenAI and Oracle data center in Saline Township. Related chairman Stephen Ross gave her the $8,325 maximum. She has pledged a statewide moratorium on new data centers. The MPSC data center tariff case and any moratorium bill land in 2027.
2. **Organized labor.** The UAW, SEIU and LIUNA each gave the $83,250 PAC maximum, and the UAW endorsed her on June 5, 2026. Building trades want the union construction jobs that data centers and state projects bring, which pulls against her moratorium pledge.
3. **Utilities.** Her campaign calls her the only candidate not taking utility money, yet her August filing shows $3,000 from DTE Energy executive chairman Gerardo Norcia. The next governor appoints the MPSC, and Proposal 2 on the November 3 ballot would ban utility political donations.
4. **Health care.** Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan chief executive Tricia Keith and former chief executive Dan Loepp both gave the maximum. The next governor runs Medicaid implementation of the 2025 federal budget law.
5. **Party money.** Gov. Whitmer's Building Bridges PAC gave $83,250 on August 20, 2026, and the DGA Victory Fund gave $80,000 on August 21, 2026, a secondary figure. A DGA associated group, Making Michigan's Future, is running ads against James.

## Committee structure and treasurer

Benson runs a state candidate committee for governor. Its exact filed name, Bureau of Elections ID and treasurer were not found in any page read for this file. In 2025 the campaign moved $1.2 million from her Secretary of State committee into the governor campaign, which is why Bridge Michigan adjusted her claimed $5.7 million 2025 total down to about $4.5 million of new money, per https://bridgemi.com/michigan-government/benson-james-duggan-grow-money-momentum-in-michigan-governor-race/. She also established Michigan Legacy PAC, which Bridge says cannot spend independently to support her candidacy, per https://bridgemi.com/michigan-government/whos-funding-michigan-governor-candidates-new-filings-reveal-top-donors/. Michigan Legacy PAC gave to her campaign in 2025 in the $10,000 to $60,000 range, per Michigan Advance on January 2, 2026, https://michiganadvance.com/2026/01/02/michigan-gubernatorial-spending-over-25m-on-pace-to-resemble-states-most-expensive-elections/.

Her money by period: $4.75 million raised through September 30, 2025, with $2.98 million on hand; $995,000 from October 21 to December 31, 2025, per Crain's Detroit, https://prod.crainsdetroit.com/node/934626; $4.9 million from January 1 to July 20, 2026 with over $6.4 million on hand, per Michigan Advance, https://michiganadvance.com/?p=109761; and more than $1.8 million from July 20 to August 24, 2026 across about 17,700 contributions averaging $102, per Bridge, https://bridgemi.com/michigan-government/jocelyn-benson-outraises-john-james-see-top-donors-in-michigan-governor-race/. Adding the two 2026 periods gives about $6.7 million raised in 2026 through August 24, a derived figure. Campaign manager is Nikki Goldschein and press secretary is Rajan Srinivasan. Former Senate Minority Leader Jim Ananich is reportedly leading her transition.

## Data centers and the Related Companies tie

**Documented.** Ryan Friedrichs is vice president of development at Related Companies, the parent of Related Digital, which is developing a 1 gigawatt class data center in Saline Township with Oracle and OpenAI, per Michigan Advance on November 12, 2025, https://michiganadvance.com/2025/11/12/michigans-benson-has-familial-professional-ties-to-company-pushing-data-center-project-in-saline/. The Detroit News reported he was a registered lobbyist for Related in Michigan, and the Benson campaign said that license was terminated in May 2025. Stephen Ross, chairman of Related and owner of the Miami Dolphins, gave Benson $8,325, per Crain's, https://prod.crainsdetroit.com/node/925231. The MPSC voted on December 18, 2025 to conditionally approve DTE Electric's special contracts for the project: a power supply agreement of about 19 years with a 20 year extension option and a 15 year storage agreement for a $7 billion, 1.4 gigawatt campus on 575 acres. The MPSC also required DTE to file a generally applicable data center tariff in a contested case, per Planet Detroit, https://planetdetroit.org/2025/12/dte-data-center-contracts-approved/. Attorney General Dana Nessel called the decision extremely disappointing. Friedrichs said in March 2026 that he would no longer work on Related's Michigan projects, per Planet Detroit, https://planetdetroit.org/2026/06/whitmer-data-center-backlash-2026-election/, and Related denies he profits from the project, per Michigan Advance on July 29, 2026.

Other tech money is small and capped: Nvidia co founder Chris Malachowsky gave $8,325 in late 2025, Google AI chief Jeff Dean gave an unreported amount, and Anduril co founder Matthew Grimm gave the legal maximum in August 2026.

**What she has said.** Her website says, "As Governor, I will put a moratorium on data centers," and that rules must make data centers "bear the cost of additional energy usage. Not the consumer," ban them from tax breaks, require public hearings, and require union contracts, per https://www.jocelynbenson.com/issues/data-centers. On October 2, 2026 in Saline Township she said James "has voted four times to block local control" and that her husband has stepped away from Michigan projects, per Michigan Public, https://www.michiganpublic.org/politics-government/2026-10-02/governors-race-hits-saline-township-site-of-massive-data-center-project.

**Contested.** James said Benson's family "has personally benefited to the tune of hundreds of thousands of dollars" from data centers. Michigan Public did not verify the claim. Benson says her husband stepped away, and Related denies he profits from the project. No filing reviewed shows a dollar figure.

Inference: The household tie runs to the developer of the single largest pending data center decision in the state, while her public position is the most restrictive in the race. Her moratorium pledge and the MPSC tariff case are the two places where that tie will be tested in 2027. A moratorium that grandfathers Saline would be the outcome to watch.

## Labor unions

**Documented.** UAW, SEIU and LIUNA each gave $83,250, the PAC maximum, by July 20, 2026, and the Michigan League of Conservation Voters gave the same, per Bridge on July 25, 2026. UFCW's Active Ballot Club gave $15,000 in late 2025. The Michigan Laborers Political League and the Michigan Regional Council of Carpenters gave in the $10,000 to $60,000 range in 2025. The UAW endorsed her on June 5, 2026 in a joint package with Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, saying "we need to elect a leader in Lansing that stands alongside the UAW against corporate interests," per https://michiganadvance.com/2026/06/08/uaw-endorsement-of-benson-el-sayed-shakes-up-gubernatorial-u-s-senate-races-in-final-stretch/.

**What they want and the lever.** The Saline project alone promises about 2,500 union construction jobs. Labor also wants the governor's posture on tariffs and auto plants, but no Benson pledge on those topics appeared in pages read.

Inference: Building trades and the environmental groups that both funded her want opposite things on data centers. Her answer so far is a moratorium paired with union contract requirements, which lets both sides read a win until a specific project comes up.

## Party and leadership money

**Documented.** Building Bridges PAC, controlled by Gov. Whitmer, gave $83,250 on August 20, 2026. The DGA Victory Fund gave $80,000 on August 21, 2026, per Hoodline citing Bridge; this is secondary. Emily's List gave $15,000 and The Next 50 PAC gave $15,000 in late 2025. Making Michigan's Future, associated with the DGA, launched an ad called Swamp against James on September 8, 2026, per Ballotpedia citing the Detroit News. Its spending total was not found.

Inference: The party is fully consolidated behind her, and the RGA's withdrawal from Michigan, reported by Bridge on October 13, 2026, means outside money now runs almost entirely in her favor.

## Own finances and disclosure history

No personal financial disclosure for Benson was located in pages read, and no third party net worth estimate was found. Her listed state salary as Secretary of State is $112,410 per Ballotpedia. Her spouse's employer, Related Companies, is the material business interest for this file. No stock trading controversy was found.

## Enforcement and controversies

1. **Auditor General voter roll review.** An Auditor General letter released August 28, 2026 found 321 elector records cancelled for citizenship from January 1, 2022 through March 30, 2026, and 18,523 registrants flagged as noncitizens in the state system. Of 25 sampled, 9 were confirmed noncitizens and none of the 9 had voting history. The auditor said the citizenship field alone is not enough to cancel a registration. The report does not include a Bureau of Elections response on these findings, per https://audgen.michigan.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/r231023726.pdf. James called it "incompetence, corruption, or both." Benson's campaign said she made Michigan "a national model for secure, transparent elections."
2. **Misprinted licenses.** Thousands of driver's licenses were misprinted. The campaign blamed a third party vendor and said the department caught the error and reissued IDs, per Michigan Public on September 9, 2026.
3. **Utility money claim.** Her campaign says she takes no utility money. Her August filing lists $3,000 from DTE executive chairman Gerardo Norcia, per Bridge on September 4, 2026. The campaign's response to that specific gift was not found.

## Deal table

| Interest | Money in | Ask | Lever | Stake | Decision date |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Related Cos., Ross, Related Digital | $8,325 Ross; spouse is Related VP | Keep Saline on track; a moratorium that exempts approved projects | Moratorium bill, MPSC appointments, data center tariff | $7B project, 1.4 GW load | 2027 session; MPSC tariff case timing not verified |
| Labor unions | $83,250 each from UAW, SEIU, LIUNA; more from Laborers, Carpenters, UFCW | Union construction jobs, project labor terms | Union contract rules in data center policy; state projects | About 2,500 Saline construction jobs | 2027 session |
| Utilities, DTE | $3,000 Norcia | Contracts and rates approved; no utility donation ban | MPSC appointments, tariff case | Grid costs of 1.4 GW and future loads | Proposal 2 on Nov 3, 2026; MPSC terms not verified |
| Health care, BCBSM | $8,325 Keith; maximum from Loepp; PharmaScript founder | Medicaid implementation choices | MDHHS direction | Not quantified | 2027 |
| Party, Whitmer, DGA | $83,250 Building Bridges; $80,000 DGA, secondary | Win the trifecta | Agenda for 2027 and 2028 | Control of Lansing | Nov 3, 2026 |

## Levers and calendar

| Decision | Who holds it now | When | Which donors care |
|---|---|---|---|
| Statewide data center moratorium | Whitmer and the Legislature | 2027 session | Related, Ross, DTE, AI donors, building trades |
| MPSC general data center tariff | MPSC | Ordered December 18, 2025 | DTE, Related Digital, Oracle, OpenAI |
| MPSC appointments | Governor | As terms expire | DTE, Consumers, MLCV |
| Proposal 2 utility donation ban | Voters | November 3, 2026 | DTE, Consumers |
| Scholarship Tax Credit opt in | Governor; Whitmer has not opted in | Early 2027 | DeVos family, on the James side |
| Medicaid changes from H.R. 1 | Governor through MDHHS | 2027 | BCBSM, SEIU |

Calendar. November 3, 2026: general election and Proposal 2. January 1, 2027: new term begins, inferred from her Secretary of State term ending that day. Early 2027: first budget, moratorium bill, Scholarship Tax Credit decision. 2027 into 2028: MPSC data center tariff contested case and appointments as terms expire. 2028: second budget and the presidential cycle, when the Saline project's power demand ramps.

## What we could not verify

Benson's candidate committee filed name, ID and treasurer; Michigan Legacy PAC's own report; the pre-general report due the week of October 19, 2026; DGA and Making Michigan's Future dollar totals; any Benson personal financial disclosure; MPSC term end dates; the Scholarship Tax Credit deadline; the dollar value of the data center tax exemption; any Proposal 2 position. Web search quota ran out midway, so these were not chased further.

URLs whose bodies were not read or did not load: https://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/politics/2024/09/24/watchdog-group-files-complaint-over-u-s-rep-james-stock-trades/75354565007/ which was blocked; https://ballotpedia.org/Michigan_2026_ballot_propositions which was blocked; https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/08/us/michigan-enhanced-ids-misprints.html; https://www.michigan.gov/mpsc/commission/events/2026/07/16/july-16-2026-commission-meeting; https://michiganadvance.com/2026/02/04/benson-raises-most-in-gubernatorial-race-in-final-2025-campaign-filings-cox-has-most-cash-on-hand/; https://www.michiganpublic.org/politics-government/2026-10-22/benson-kicks-off-statewide-bus-tour-aims-to-reclaim-lansing-trifecta; https://www.bridgedetroit.com/?p=234712; https://www.michiganpublic.org/politics-government/2025-09-07/michigan-midterm-campaigns-projected-to-be-second-most-expensive-in-country. The DGA Victory Fund $80,000 figure was read only in Hoodline, https://hoodline.com/2026/09/benson-banks-5-9m-war-chest-leaves-james-scrambling-with-just-1-5m/, and is Secondary.

# Jocelyn Benson research notes

Audit trail for the compact Tier 2 file. Compiled October 23, 2026. Web search quota was exhausted after about 10 searches shared across subjects, so later threads relied on fetching pages already found and links inside them.

## Thread 1: Committees and totals

**Takeaway.** Capped, broad money. About $6.7 million raised in 2026 through August 24, derived, plus 2025 receipts that include a $1.2 million transfer from her Secretary of State committee. $5.9 million cash on hand August 24.

**Cited findings.**
1. Through Sept 30, 2025: $4.75M raised, $1.76M spent, $2.98M on hand. https://michiganadvance.com/2026/01/02/michigan-gubernatorial-spending-over-25m-on-pace-to-resemble-states-most-expensive-elections/ read January 2, 2026 article. Also says full report not downloadable because of volume, and that her husband is a Related VP.
2. Oct 21 to Dec 31, 2025: $995,000, cash $3.5M plus. https://prod.crainsdetroit.com/node/934626 undated Crain's article.
3. Bridge, February 2, 2026: nearly $1M in the period, campaign claimed $5.7M for 2025 including $1.2M transferred from SOS committee, adjusted about $4.5M; about 4,400 donors averaging $137. https://bridgemi.com/michigan-government/benson-james-duggan-grow-money-momentum-in-michigan-governor-race/
4. Jan 1 to Jul 20, 2026: about $5M raised, cash over $6.4M; Michigan Legacy PAC established by Benson. https://bridgemi.com/michigan-government/whos-funding-michigan-governor-candidates-new-filings-reveal-top-donors/ Michigan Advance gives $4.9M raised and $2.1M spent. https://michiganadvance.com/?p=109761
5. Jul 20 to Aug 24, 2026: more than $1.8M raised, about 17,700 contributions averaging $102, just over $1M from Michigan, $5.9M on hand. https://bridgemi.com/michigan-government/jocelyn-benson-outraises-john-james-see-top-donors-in-michigan-governor-race/ Hoodline adds $2.3M spent. https://hoodline.com/2026/09/benson-banks-5-9m-war-chest-leaves-james-scrambling-with-just-1-5m/
6. Ad booking heading into October: Benson and allies about $23M versus James about $1M, AdImpact. RGA withdrew nearly all reserved time. https://bridgemi.com/michigan-government/can-john-james-close-the-gap-on-jocelyn-benson-in-the-michigan-governors-race/

**Inferences.** The headline 2026 figure is derived by adding two non overlapping periods; Bridge and Michigan Advance differ by $100,000 on the first period.

**Gaps.** Filed committee name, ID, treasurer, top vendors and media buyer. Pre-general report not reviewed.

## Thread 2: Data centers, Related Companies, utilities

**Takeaway.** Spouse works for the developer of the Saline data center; Benson pledges a moratorium. DTE executive chairman gave $3,000 despite the no utility money claim.

**Cited findings.**
1. Friedrichs is VP of Development at Related; Related Digital developing Saline with Oracle and OpenAI; Detroit News reported he was a registered lobbyist, campaign says license terminated in May; Ross gave $8,325 in July filing; campaign manager Nikki Goldschein quote on electricity bills and water. https://michiganadvance.com/2025/11/12/michigans-benson-has-familial-professional-ties-to-company-pushing-data-center-project-in-saline/
2. MPSC vote December 18, 2025 conditionally approving DTE special contracts, 19 year supply with 20 year option, 15 year storage, $7B, 1.4 GW, 575 acres, contested case for general data center tariff; Nessel extremely disappointed. https://planetdetroit.org/2025/12/dte-data-center-contracts-approved/
3. Friedrichs said in March 2026 he would no longer work on Related Michigan projects; Whitmer signed data center sales and use tax exemptions in early 2025; groundbreaking June 1, 2026. https://planetdetroit.org/2026/06/whitmer-data-center-backlash-2026-election/
4. Benson pledge text: moratorium, data centers bear energy cost, no tax breaks, public hearings, union contracts. https://www.jocelynbenson.com/issues/data-centers
5. October 2, 2026 Saline event: Benson says James voted four times to block local control and her husband stepped away; James says her family benefited by hundreds of thousands, unverified; correction October 3 that candidates do not differ on repealing tax breaks. https://www.michiganpublic.org/politics-government/2026-10-02/governors-race-hits-saline-township-site-of-massive-data-center-project
6. Related denies Friedrichs profits. https://michiganadvance.com/?p=109761
7. Norcia $3,000; Keith $8,325; Loepp, Grimm and University of Michigan regent Denise Ilitch, spelled Denish Illitch in the fetched text, at the maximum; Building Bridges $83,250; Proposal 2 would ban utility donations; campaign calls her only candidate not taking utility money. https://bridgemi.com/michigan-government/jocelyn-benson-outraises-john-james-see-top-donors-in-michigan-governor-race/
8. Malachowsky, Ven Johnson, Edsel Ford II, Cynthia Ford, Jennifer Pritzker at $8,325; Emily's List, Next 50, UFCW at $15,000. https://prod.crainsdetroit.com/node/934626
9. Ross, Kircher, Torgow, McLaren, Oberheide, George and Alex Soros, Save Democracy PAC, Next 50 PAC at $8,325. https://prod.crainsdetroit.com/node/925231 undated.

**Inferences.** A moratorium that grandfathers approved projects would protect Saline. Which way she goes is the clearest test of the household tie.

**Gaps.** Friedrichs compensation; any Related or Related Digital lobbying registrations; MPSC tariff case number and schedule; MPSC term dates; Proposal 2 text and Benson position.

## Thread 3: Labor and party

**Takeaway.** UAW, SEIU, LIUNA and MLCV each at the $83,250 cap; UAW endorsement June 5, 2026; Whitmer PAC and DGA in by late August.

**Cited findings.**
1. PAC maximums and top individuals Gates, Siblani, Harris, Harper, Simons. https://bridgemi.com/michigan-government/whos-funding-michigan-governor-candidates-new-filings-reveal-top-donors/
2. UAW endorsement with El-Sayed and quotes. https://michiganadvance.com/2026/06/08/uaw-endorsement-of-benson-el-sayed-shakes-up-gubernatorial-u-s-senate-races-in-final-stretch/
3. 2025 PACs in $10,000 to $60,000 range: Laborers Political League, Michigan Legacy PAC, End Citizens United, Deldin Law PAC, UFCW, Emily's List, Carpenters; maximum individuals Turfah, Brzoznowski, Tellem, Efroymson, Cassin, Lam, Ross. https://michiganadvance.com/2026/01/02/michigan-gubernatorial-spending-over-25m-on-pace-to-resemble-states-most-expensive-elections/
4. DGA Victory Fund $80,000 August 21. Hoodline only. Secondary.
5. Making Michigan's Future, DGA associated, Swamp ad September 8, 2026. https://ballotpedia.org/Michigan_gubernatorial_election,_2026

**Inferences.** Labor and environmental funders want opposite outcomes on data centers; her policy mixes a moratorium and union contract rules.

**Gaps.** UAW and DGA independent spending totals; MEA position on the governor race.

## Thread 4: Own finances and enforcement

**Takeaway.** No disclosure or net worth found. Main controversies are administrative and come from her Secretary of State record.

**Cited findings.**
1. Auditor General letter August 28, 2026: 321 citizenship cancellations, 18,523 flagged, 9 of 25 confirmed noncitizens, none with voting history; no agency response on these findings. https://audgen.michigan.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/r231023726.pdf
2. James attack and Benson campaign response on audit and misprinted licenses. https://www.michiganpublic.org/politics-government/2026-09-10/republicans-and-democrats-hurling-attacks-and-counter-attacks-in-michigan-governors-race
3. Ballotpedia: SOS since January 1, 2019; term ends January 1, 2027; salary $112,410; 2022 SOS contributions $5,280,541. https://ballotpedia.org/Jocelyn_Benson

**Inferences.** None beyond the profile.

**Gaps.** Michigan personal financial disclosure filings; any ethics complaints or lawsuits against her personally.
